_metadata.grading: numeric widths only; the closed form in (m_V,m_1,m_2) is unwieldy (no formula stage)
_metadata.verification: vertex validated against the literature Z'->W+W- closed form at m_V/m = 3, 5, 10 and 300 (rel <1e-9, the check that discriminates the all-incoming momentum assignment); each width then computed by two independent contractions (explicit polarization vectors vs completeness-tensor einsum) agreeing <1e-9; longitudinal m_V^5/(m1^2 m2^2) scaling checked
_metadata.convention: YM triple-gauge vertex with ALL-INCOMING momenta (k1+k2+k3=0); for P -> q1 q2 that is (P, -q1, -q2). The as-drawn (P, q1, q2) assignment is the vertex outside its domain and gives widths low by ~2.9x at these mass ratios.
citations: J.L. Hewett, T.G. Rizzo, Phys.Rept. 183 (1989) 193 (Z' -> W+W- and heavy-vector decays)
M.E. Peskin, D.V. Schroeder, An Introduction to QFT, ch. 16 (Yang-Mills triple-gauge vertex)
